sections.h2: Where is Fayetteville, Arkansas, and what is the terrain like?
sections.html:
Fayetteville is the county seat of Washington County, in the Ozarks of Northwest Arkansas, at the edge of the Boston Mountains. The city stands at about 1,378 feet of elevation and covers roughly 55 square miles.

Settlers arrived around 1828, and the town was incorporated on November 3, 1836. The Civil War left a mark: Union forces under General Samuel Curtis occupied the town in February 1862, retreating Confederates burned their arsenal and much of the town, and the Action at Fayetteville followed on April 18, 1863.

Hilly ground matters when you sell. Slopes, steep driveways, retaining walls and older foundations on Mount Sequoyah or near the Square draw closer inspection than a flat lot would.

sections.h2: How do the University of Arkansas and other employers shape the housing market?
sections.html:
The University of Arkansas is the largest employer in Fayetteville and the biggest single influence on housing demand. It opened on January 22, 1872, as Arkansas Industrial University and took its present name in 1899. Fall 2021 enrollment passed 29,000, a record at that time, according to the university.

A 2020 ranking of the city's top employers lists:

  • University of Arkansas
  • Washington Regional Medical Center
  • Walmart
  • Fayetteville School District
  • Veterans Administration Medical Center
  • City of Fayetteville
  • APAC Central, Pinnacle Foods, Tyson Foods and Washington County government

Walmart and J.B. Hunt are headquartered nearby, and Tyson is based in neighboring Springdale. Regional corporate jobs feed the buyer pool, while the university feeds the rental pool. Owners of student rentals often sell after a lease ends or after a long vacancy.

sections.h2: Which Fayetteville areas do sellers talk about?
sections.html:
Local descriptions divide the city by the major roads and the campus. The areas include:

  • West Fayetteville, the part of town west of I-49/US 71.
  • Uptown, near the Northwest Arkansas Mall in the north.
  • Dickson Street, the entertainment district next to campus.
  • The historic Square, the original center of the city.
  • East Fayetteville, east of US 71B, which includes homes on Mount Sequoyah.
  • South Fayetteville, south of Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard.

Wilson Park, Mount Nord and Washington-Willow are the named historic districts. A house in one of them can come with design expectations from neighbors and the city, so ask the planning office before you plan exterior changes you want to make before a sale.

sections.h2: Which school district serves Fayetteville homes?
sections.html:
Fayetteville Public Schools serves most of the city. The district was established in 1871 and runs eight elementary schools, four intermediate schools, two special schools and Fayetteville High School.

Buyers with children often check attendance zones before they make an offer, so write down the zoned schools for your address and confirm them with the district. A few edges of the city may sit in other districts, which the district office can confirm.

Other public employers also matter to the housing market, including the Veterans Administration medical center and city and county government, which keep a steady base of year-round residents apart from the student population.

sections.h2: What roads and transit connect Fayetteville to the region?
sections.html:
Interstate 49, which carries US 71, is the city's main through route. It was formerly I-540, and the redesignation to I-49 was approved on March 28, 2014. College Avenue, the old US 71B, remains a commercial spine.

The Razorback Greenway is a 36-mile, mostly off-road shared-use trail that links Fayetteville with Bella Vista through Johnson, Springdale, Lowell, Bentonville and Rogers. Homes with easy trail access often highlight it in listings.

Northwest Arkansas National Airport, which opened in 1998, is about 17 miles northwest of the city. Drake Field, the municipal airport, handles general aviation and many Razorback team charters.

sections.h2: What does Fayetteville weather mean for an older house?
sections.html:
July highs average near 89 degrees and January lows near 27, and the city sees about 47 inches of precipitation a year with an average of 3.3 snowy days.

Extremes are larger than the averages. The city's record high is 111 degrees, set on July 14, 1954, and its record low is minus 24 on February 12, 1899. Pipes in unheated crawlspaces and older roofs are the usual trouble spots after a hard winter.

Before a sale, buyers tend to ask about the age of the roof, the HVAC system and the water heater, so have receipts ready.

sections.h2: What are Fayetteville's short-term rental rules?
sections.html:
Fayetteville requires a permit to operate a short-term rental, and the rules began phasing in during 2021 and early 2022. The city defines two types: Type I, where full-time occupants live on the property and rent a room or addition nightly, and Type II, where guests stay nightly and no one lives there full time.

Applicants needed a business license, a building safety inspection, proof of ownership, an insurance review, sales tax filings and a landlord registry listing. In January 2022 the city had received 376 applications and approved 177, and officials estimated 500 to 600 rentals operated in the city. The council also widened the zones where they are allowed.

If you own a rental that has a permit, ask the planning office whether it transfers to a new owner before you promise it to a buyer.

sections.h2: How do property taxes work for a Fayetteville seller?
sections.html:
Washington County bills real estate tax, due by October 15 each year. Payments after that date draw a 10% penalty, and real estate also accrues 10% annual interest, according to the county collector.

You can pay online by credit card, which carries a processing fee, in person, or by mail using the instructions on your annual statement. For statement questions the collector lists 479-444-1526. The collector's page does not explain proration at a sale, so ask the title company how the current year's tax will be divided at closing.

Arkansas also charges a real property transfer tax of $3.30 per $1,000 of the price, which the state Department of Finance and Administration administers.

sections.h2: Selling for cash in Fayetteville: when it fits
sections.html:
A cash sale fits Fayetteville owners who want certainty more than the highest price on a listing. Typical cases include a house that needs work the owner cannot fund, an inherited property in another owner's name, a landlord leaving the rental business, or a move that has a firm date.

Compare each path on net proceeds and timing. A listing in a competitive market can bring more, but only after repairs, showings and a buyer's financing clear. A cash offer trades some of that upside for a closing date you can plan around.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to sell a short-term rental in Fayetteville?
faqs.a: You do not need a permit to sell, but the permit status matters to a buyer. Ask the city's planning office whether the permit stays with the property or the new owner must apply.

faqs.q: When are Washington County property taxes due?
faqs.a: October 15 each year. After that date a 10% penalty applies, and real estate tax also accrues 10% annual interest, per the county collector.

faqs.q: What is the Arkansas transfer tax on a house sale?
faqs.a: It is $3.30 per $1,000 of the actual consideration on deeds that convey real estate. The purchase contract states which party pays it.

faqs.q: Is Fayetteville a good place to sell a rental near campus?
faqs.a: Demand comes from the University of Arkansas and regional employers, which helps. Timing matters, since a vacant unit during the school year is harder to show.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Fayetteville house that needs major repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A buyer purchasing for cash can take it as it is. Get written offers and compare them to the net from a repaired listing.
